preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n.is_integer() and 3 <= n <= 200000 for n in (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line contains an integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) representing the length of array a, where a_i = i. The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_lines) == 1 + m for m, *ops in (line.split() for line in stdout_lines if line.strip()) for stdout_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+1+m] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), 1)])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first line of output is an integer m (m ≤ n + 5) representing the number of operations. The following m lines each contain two integers x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n; x ≠ y) representing the indices of the operation.

postconditions.expression: all(len(ops) == m and all(x.is_integer() and y.is_integer() and 1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for x, y in ops) for m, *ops in (line.split() for line in stdout_lines if line.strip()) for stdout_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+1+m] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), 1)])
postconditions.description: Each operation pair (x, y) is valid: indices x and y are within bounds (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n) and distinct (x ≠ y).

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(a[i] == 1 for i in range(1, n+1) if i != target) and a[target] == 2 for target in range(1, n+1)) for n, *ops in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]),) + (tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+m]) for i, m in enumerate([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])] for a in [list(range(1, n+1))] for _ in ops for a in [a[:] for _ in range(1)] for x, y in ops for a in [a[:] for _ in range(1)] for a[x-1] in [ceil(a[x-1] / a[y-1])] for a in [a[:]])
postconditions.description: After applying all operations to the initial array a = [1, 2, ..., n], the resulting array contains exactly n-1 ones and 1 two. The operations transform the array as per the ceiling division rule: a_x = ceil(a_x / a_y) for each operation (x, y).
